Define marketplace success beyond clicks: qualified applications, recruiter response, successful matches, and applicant experience. Build a candidate-generation layer using job text/skills/location embeddings plus explicit eligibility constraints. Content features make new jobs retrievable before interaction history exists. Log impressions and position so click/application labels are interpretable.

Rank with shared representations and separate click, apply, and downstream-success heads; hire labels are delayed and selectively observed, so use maturity windows and model missingness rather than calling every unobserved hire a negative. Calibrate task outputs and combine them with business utility and eligibility rules.

A final constrained reranker can limit concentration of exposure/applications, spread opportunities, and respect recruiter capacity. Define fairness metrics and relevant cohorts before optimization; blindly equalizing clicks can damage matching. Online updates should include recent searches and dismissed jobs. Evaluate application quality, applicant/job coverage, recruiter overload, and long-term outcomes in randomized experiments. Maintain content-based fallbacks for cold starts and stale feature stores.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** Ranking for expected qualified matches can use an illustrative utility $P(application|x)P(qualified\ response|application,x)$, with explicit eligibility constraints. These factors must be estimated from appropriately exposed data, not treated as known probabilities. Evaluate marketplace and subgroup outcomes because optimizing clicks can increase low-quality applications or distort opportunity allocation.
